institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that were available at the host university were interesting and fit in with my study. I chose HKUST, not only because of its broad selection of courses, but also because they are known for its great knowledge, expertise, and research within the biochemical field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The best decision I've ever made. Met the most amazing people from all over the world and made friendships for life. Besides this, it was an incredible opportunity to get insight into other cultures.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. They had before the arrival sent out documents on how to check in at the dorm halls and how to get to the school etc. Besides this, there was also created a WhatsApp group with all of the exchange students and the organizers, where you could ask whatever questions you might have.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Did not receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: On the day of the check-in, there was an orientation meeting where they introduced you to different things that were a "Must Know" in Hong Kong and at school. After the meeting a student would show you around the campus, showing you the canteens and the different facilities.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared dorm rooms. You shared with another boy or girl depending on your gender. The shared dorm rooms could either be on campus or a little bit outside of campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Different canteens/shops on campus, which were open until 9-10 pm. 
On each floor in the different dorm halls, there was a common room with a microwave and a fountain that could make both boiling and cold water. Some common rooms had stoves, but my did not.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You have to buy all cleaning materials etc yourself, except for the vacuum cleaner which you can borrow from the reception. It does not get cleaned between each student. It was very dirty when I moved in, but my roomate and I cleaned it together and found a way of making it fun.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They provided a guide on how to enroll in the courses and how to use the website. They were also very helpful regarding whatever questions you might have

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You log into this website and search for the course by using a course code. Then you enroll in the course. You can either be waitlisted or enrolled straight away. If you are waitlisted you are not guaranteed to get a spot, it depends on how many students are in front of you. 
When you get enrolled, the add/drop period starts. This is where you can try out the course and see whether you like it or not. If you don’t like it, you just drop it and add another course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The faculty members and the planners of the exchange program along with the step-by-step guide.
The professors do a lot to try and enroll as many students as possible, so it helps if you talk to them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was pre-enrolled in two courses from home. Unfortunately, two of the courses I originally wanted were not available during the fall semester, but luckily HKUST had a lot of other cool courses. I found two other courses I wanted and got enrolled in them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have some backup courses in mind. If you get waitlisted and don’t make it into the course, it makes it less stressful if you already have a backup. Also, you can enroll in as many courses as you want if you don’t know which course you like. You just have to drop some of them during the add/drop period to get the required amount of 'points'

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
three of my courses was 4th year courses, which is the last year of the bachelor. 
one of my courses was a 2nd year course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There were only lectures, no examinations classes where you solved problems or stuff like that. 
There was a midterm exam, which I had never tried before either. This counts as a part of your final grade. The final grade is also determined by different assignments or presentations you hand in during the semester along with the midterm and the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Genetics and Personalized Medicine (4th year course)
Biochemistry of Diseases (4th year course)
Neurochemistry (4th year course)
Modern Approaches to Biochemical and Cellbiological Research (2nd year course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biochemistry of disease because the course teaches you the clinical manifestation and pathophysiology of common human diseases, with an emphasis on the biochemical basis underlying the development of the diseases and their treatments with drugs. This was interesting and the professor was amazing. He took his time explaining the different concepts and made sure that everybody understood what was going on.

Human Genetics and Personalized Medicine because the course teaches you the principles and up-to-date technologies for the discovery and analysis of human genetic variations. You learn how genetic factors can determine many variations in the human population such as hair thickness, tolerance to milk in adults, high blood cholesterol, and susceptibility to certain types of cancer. The professors in this course were very good too. It is a smaller course, which makes it easier to ask questions and interact with the professors. They took their time explaining the concepts and figures, making sure that it was understood by everyone.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You spend way more money on transport than you expect. The campus is outside of the center and the buses/metros stop going at 1 am, therefore if you are on a night out or just having a late dinner you need to take either an Uber or taxi home back to campus.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food on campus was very cheap. Grocery shopping at the supermarket on campus was very expensive compared with the supermarkets in town.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Different clubs like board games and different sports (such as tennis, handball, football, etc) but also clubs for different martial arts such as Kendall, taekwondo, etc. 
The school of Science (the faculty I was enrolled at) made a lot of social activities you could join such as a 'sunset tour on Victoria Harbor' or 'authentic dinner' at a local restaurant.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the events by 'Spark Global'. It's a school organization that hosts events and tours. It can be everything from a hike to a dinner or a neon party. It's a good way to meet the locals or other students from some of the other faculties.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spend the weekends or holidays exploring the amazing nature and culture of Hong Kong. Leave campus and go do something fun, whether it’s going out to eat, going to the beach, or going shopping. Hong Kong has it all.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Hong Kong is very Western, despite it being a part of China. Everyone speaks English very well and is very easy to communicate with. At the school, there are a lot of foreigners, not just exchange students but also full-time students from other countries, which also makes it easier to fit in and adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are a bit shy but want to talk to you. You should just approach them and say hello. Attend the Spark Global events, because it's a very easy way to meet and socialize with the local students. During the courses, you also have to do some group projects or presentations, which also makes it possible for you to mingle with your fellow local peers.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that you eat rice every single day. They don’t eat many fresh vegetables or salads

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way everyone is very helpful. No matter who you ask everyone is always more than happy to help you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don’t worry, you will get friends. The host institution plans a lot of activities in the first couple of days to make sure that you get to meet some of the other exchange students and make some friends.
2) Join some of the sports- or activities clubs. it’s a good way to meet new people and get to know the locals
3) If you can choose between living on campus or in the 'Jockey Club' choose on campus. It is gonna save you on days you wake up too late, and you don’t have to transport yourself to and from school every day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy an ESIM instead of a physical SIM card. It is way easier and you can buy it for the amount of days you are in Hong Kong instead of having to change the physical one every month.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All of the amazing people I have met and the experiences I got to have with them. 
Getting to be taught by some of the best professors in the field of biochemistry.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coming out of my comfort zone and taking the step of going. Leaving Copenhagen all by myself to go to a country on the other side of the world, knowing no one. But it’s been the best choice I've ever made. I have grown so much and learned so much about myself along with getting the chance to have some amazing courses with excellent teachers.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
